# Fire brigade, civil police and building rules (`fire_brigade_police_building_codes`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/institutions.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Institutions, law & governance (`institutions`)
- Deps: helped by piston_pump, fired_brick_ceramics, insurance
- Core idea: Three linked city services. A permanent paid fire watch patrols at night and keeps buckets, ladders, hooks for pulling down houses, pumps and hoses ready, with authority to demolish in the fire's path. Building rules remove the fuel: brick or stone party walls rising above the roof, tile instead of thatch, wide streets, safe chimneys and ovens, a height limit. A civil police, in uniform but separate from the army, patrols to prevent crime and answers to a court. Cities that lacked these burned every generation.
- Pitfalls:
  - Volunteers summoned by bell arrive late and untrained; a standing watch is the point
  - Rules without inspectors and penalties are ignored the day after the fire; London kept its 1667 brick rule only because surveyors enforced it
  - Nobody dares pull down houses for a firebreak without clear authority and compensation (the Lord Mayor's hesitation in London, 1666)
  - Using soldiers or secret informers as police makes the force hated and useless for ordinary crime
  - Wooden pipes and hand squirts cannot reach a roof: a force pump with a leather hose is the decisive tool
- History: mesopotamia: c. 1754 BC – Hammurabi §§229–233: the builder answers with his life or purse if his house collapses; egypt: New Kingdom – the Medjay serve as a police force guarding towns, tombs and frontiers; rome: AD 6 – Augustus founds the vigiles, seven cohorts of freedmen as night watch and firemen; height limits; after the fire of 64 Nero orders wider streets and fire-resistant stone; china: 11th–13th c. – Song Kaifeng and Hangzhou have watchtowers, guard posts at intervals and soldier-firemen with buckets, hooks and ladders; islamic: 7th–8th c. – the shurta (police) under Umayyad and Abbasid governors; the muhtasib enforces building and market rules; east_asia: 1643 – daimyo fire companies in Edo; 1718–1720 townsmen's brigades (machi-bikeshi); europe: 1667 – London Rebuilding Act requires brick and stone; 1667 Paris lieutenant of police; 1672 Jan van der Heyden's fire engine with flexible hose, Amsterdam; 1824 Edinburgh's municipal fire brigade (Braidwood); 1829 London Metropolitan Police (Peel); americas: 1736 – Franklin's volunteer Union Fire Company, Philadelphia
